root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the suffix-copy `memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, ...)`, once `if (strlen(opt))` admits the remaining tail, the number of source bytes read from `opt` must match that tail length `strlen(opt)` instead of a stale distance back to `o_org`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the suffix copy with `opt` already advanced to the one-byte tail while `o_org` still aliases the start of the duplicated option buffer. The missing source-level obligation is that the copy-count argument for bytes read from `opt` must equal `strlen(opt)` at this call site; the vulnerable original uses 5 while only 1 suffix byte remains, and the fixed original reaches the same protected event with `copy_len == strlen(opt) == 1`.

nodes.state: At the crashing `memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1)` sink, the source pointer `opt` is already the post-keyword suffix pointer while the requested read length 5 exceeds the remaining suffix length 1, so the read crosses the right edge of the 8-byte heap buffer allocated for `$ncpus\xff\0`.

edges.relation: The post-keyword suffix pointer `opt` observed immediately before the copy is the same pointer later passed to `memcpy` as its source argument.
The saved original-buffer base `o_org` observed immediately before the copy is the same base pointer still used at the sink when evaluating the stale length expression `opt - o_org - 1`.
